title: Famous Landmark
clues: I was created for a major world exhibition.
Many artists of my day signed a letter begging for me to be torn down.
I am made primarily from iron, and I grow slightly taller on hot days.
I stand beside the River Seine.
I am the wrought-iron tower that defines the skyline of Paris.

title: Famous Place
clues: I am part of a major mountain range.
People pay tens of thousands of dollars for a chance to stand on me.
My summit sits in the jet stream, where the air holds a third of the oxygen you are breathing now.
I lie on the border between Nepal and Tibet.
I am Earth's highest mountain above sea level.

title: Amazing Animal
clues: I am a mammal, and I have the digestive system of a carnivore.
I spend up to fourteen hours a day eating.
My diet is almost entirely one particular fast-growing grass.
I am a national treasure of China, and I am loaned to zoos rather than sold.
I am the bear famous for my black-and-white fur.

title: Space Mystery
clues: Humans have watched me and kept calendars by me for thousands of years.
I pull on Earth's oceans twice a day.
I have almost no atmosphere, so footprints left on me can last for millions of years.
Twelve people have walked on my surface.
I am Earth's only natural satellite.

title: Famous Invention
clues: My arrival changed the way people communicate forever.
My early versions needed a human operator to physically connect two people.
Alexander Graham Bell is credited with my first practical patent, in 1876.
For a century I hung on walls with a cord and a rotary dial.
I let two people speak to each other from far apart, and today you carry me in your pocket.

title: Famous Food
clues: I started as cheap street food for working people in Italy.
Arguments about what belongs on top of me can end friendships.
I am traditionally baked in a wood-fired oven at around 450 degrees Celsius.
My most famous version is named after a queen: tomato, mozzarella and basil.
I am round, flat, sliced into wedges, and Naples is my birthplace.

title: Movie Mystery
clues: I am built around a famous real-life disaster.
A very large ship plays a central role in my story.
My love story crosses a sharp divide of social class.
James Cameron directed me, and I won eleven Academy Awards.
My name is the name of the ship that sank in 1912.

title: Technology Mystery
clues: I began as a university research project run out of a garage.
My first product helped people find things they could not otherwise find.
My name turned into a verb that people use every day.
I also own the world's largest video platform.
My parent company is called Alphabet, and my name is a misspelling of a very large number.

title: Ancient Wonder
clues: I was finished roughly 4,500 years ago.
I held the record as the tallest structure made by humans for over 3,800 years.
I am built from millions of enormous limestone blocks.
I am the only surviving member of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.
I am the largest of the three pyramids standing on the Giza plateau in Egypt.

title: Everyday Technology
clues: I connect billions of people and devices.
I grew out of a military research network called ARPANET.
I move information as packets that can each take a different route.
Websites, email and video calls all ride on top of me.
I am the global network of interconnected computer networks.

title: City Mystery
clues: I was once the richest trading power in my part of the world.
I am built on soft ground, and I am slowly sinking.
I have no cars in my historic centre - deliveries arrive by boat.
My most famous boat is a slim black one steered by a standing rower.
I am the Italian city of canals, gondolas and St Mark's Square.

title: Country Mystery
clues: I am an island nation made up of thousands of islands.
I closed myself off from most of the world for over 200 years.
I sit on the Ring of Fire, so earthquakes shape how I build everything.
My bullet trains are famous for being measured in seconds, not minutes.
My flag is a red circle on white, and my capital is Tokyo.

title: Sport Mystery
clues: I was invented indoors, on purpose, to keep students active during winter.
My inventor's first version used two peach baskets and a soccer ball.
Five players per side take the court at a time.
Scoring from beyond a certain arc is worth an extra point.
My most famous league is the NBA, and the hoop stands ten feet high.

title: Turning Point in History
clues: I happened suddenly, and almost nobody predicted my exact date.
I began partly because of a confused announcement at a press conference.
Crowds attacked concrete with hammers and chisels, and kept the pieces as souvenirs.
I marked the beginning of the end of the Cold War, in November 1989.
I am the night a divided German city tore down the barrier that split it in two.

title: Famous Object
clues: My inventor was an architecture professor who built me as a teaching tool.
It took my own inventor a month to solve me the first time.
I have roughly 43 quintillion possible arrangements.
Any arrangement of me can be solved in 20 moves or fewer.
I am the six-sided colour puzzle you twist until every face matches.

title: Extreme Survivor
clues: I am a bird, but I have never flown a day in my life.
I can dive deeper than 500 metres and hold my breath for over 20 minutes.
We huddle in enormous crowds and rotate positions so nobody freezes on the outside.
The father balances the single egg on his feet through the polar winter.
I am the largest penguin, and I live in Antarctica.

title: Iconic Dish
clues: I began as a way to preserve fish, not as a delicacy.
My defining ingredient is not the fish - it is the seasoned rice.
I became fast food sold at street stalls in old Edo.
I am often served with wasabi, pickled ginger and soy sauce.
I am the Japanese dish of vinegared rice, often topped or rolled with raw fish.

title: Invisible Technology
clues: I was built by a military, then opened up to everyone on Earth for free.
I depend on a constellation of satellites orbiting about 20,000 km up.
I only work because my atomic clocks are corrected for Einstein's relativity.
You need signals from at least four of my satellites to pin down a position.
I am the system in your phone that tells you exactly where you are.

title: Planet Mystery
clues: I am a gas giant with no solid surface to stand on.
I am so light for my size that I would float in a big enough bathtub of water.
I have well over a hundred known moons, including one with lakes of liquid methane.
The Cassini spacecraft spent 13 years studying me before diving into my clouds.
I am the planet famous for my spectacular rings of ice and rock.

title: Blockbuster Mystery
clues: I am based on a bestselling novel by Michael Crichton.
My most famous moment of dread involves a glass of water and a ripple.
Steven Spielberg directed me, and I changed visual effects forever.
My plot turns on cloning ancient creatures from DNA trapped in amber.
I am the 1993 film about a dinosaur theme park that goes very wrong.

title: Brand Mystery
clues: I am a family business founded in a small Danish town in 1932.
I started out making wooden toys, and my workshop burned down more than once.
My name comes from two Danish words meaning 'play well'.
By sheer number of units produced, I am one of the largest tyre makers in the world.
My interlocking plastic bricks from 1958 still snap onto the ones made today.

title: Famous Building
clues: My winning design was pulled back out of a competition's reject pile.
I ran ten years late and more than fourteen times over budget.
My architect resigned partway through and never saw me finished.
My shells are clad in over a million white and cream tiles, and I sit on a harbour.
I am the sail-shaped performing arts centre on Bennelong Point in Sydney.

title: World-Changing Invention
clues: Before me, copying a single book could take a scribe a year.
I borrowed my key mechanism from wine and olive presses.
My breakthrough was movable metal type that could be rearranged endlessly.
Johannes Gutenberg built me in Mainz around 1440.
I am the machine that made books cheap and put mass literacy within reach.

title: Natural Wonder
clues: I span nine countries, though most of me sits in one.
I generate much of my own rainfall - my trees breathe out rivers of vapour.
Roughly one in ten known species on Earth lives inside me.
The river running through me discharges more water than the next several largest rivers combined.
I am the vast South American rainforest named after that river.

title: Modern Metropolis
clues: I am a city, an island and a country all at once.
I became independent in 1965, not by choice but by separation.
I have four official languages and almost no natural resources of my own.
My port is one of the busiest on the planet, and my airport keeps winning awards.
My skyline features a hotel topped by a boat, and my mascot is a lion with a fish's tail.
